lens: mobile task completion, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and recovery

findings.observation: On iPhone 17 in English AX5, People job/company text approaches the name's scale and darkness. Nia's four-line job/company block occupies much more visual area than her name. Bold still distinguishes identity, so this is a small refinement rather than a task failure or an objection to scrolling.
findings.evidence: round-3/08-people-ax5.png: Leila Hartmann followed by VP Product · Meridian Labs. round-3/10-people-ax5-scrolled.png: Nia Williams followed by the large Operating Partner · Northlight Capital block. Inspect these full uncropped viewports at the stated first/later positions.
findings.user_impact: Supported inference: when scanning a long person record at AX5, the role/company block can compete with the identity that anchors retrieval. No measured slowdown is claimed.
findings.recommendation: Use a modestly quieter semantic hierarchy for the job/company block while retaining full Dynamic Type scaling, complete context, and natural scrolling.
findings.verification: Compare uncropped People screenshots at default and AX5, then observe a find-and-reopen task; verify name-first scanning and access to complete identity, company, and search context without line limits or a fixed font cap.

findings.observation: At AX5 the fixed global Ask anything composer remains a second broad rounded input surface beside the task-specific Search control. Its wording is distinct, but its visual weight persists through retrieval scrolling.
findings.evidence: round-3/07-sessions-ax5.png and round-3/08-people-ax5.png show the top Search field and bottom Ask anything composer together; round-3/10-people-ax5-scrolled.png shows the same composer at the later People position. Device/state: iPhone 17, portrait, English AX5.
findings.user_impact: Subjective craft inference: the shell offers a competing input destination while the recruiter is trying to reopen a known item. No wrong-input event or inaccessible content is demonstrated.
findings.recommendation: Explore a lower-emphasis global composer presentation during retrieval scrolling while keeping its route accessible and preserving search/filter functions.
findings.verification: Observe retrieval tasks in the full shell at AX5 and verify all controls remain discoverable and hittable. Keep the existing treatment if the alternative adds friction or obscures an essential control.

findings.observation: The light unread card's diffuse shadow produces a broad halo even though the surface and explicit Unread text already distinguish that state. The dark unread state uses a quieter tonal treatment.
findings.evidence: round-3/02-sessions-unread-light.png: Leila's white unread card and soft halo below its lower edge. round-3/05-sessions-dark-zh.png: Nia's tonal unread card with explicit 未读. Device/state: iPhone 17 default text, English light versus Chinese dark.
findings.user_impact: Subjective material refinement: the halo adds a little visual emphasis beyond the operational meaning. Read/unread and review attention are still distinguishable; no ranking of a person is inferred.
findings.recommendation: Slightly reduce light unread shadow spread/intensity while retaining explicit unread wording and a distinct surface.
findings.verification: Inspect full light/dark screenshots of read, unread-only, review-only, and combined states; verify unread stays clear without relying on shadow or color alone.

strengths: Bounded task and evidence: independent recruiter reopening a conversation/person on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5, portrait, synthetic data, English light and Chinese dark, default and English AX5. All ten round-3 PNGs were inspected uncropped. Evidence ladder level 4 with an attributed written native-check summary; no direct interaction by this reviewer. The 3/4 score applies to this bounded retrieval review, not a complete capture-to-action release approval.

Task legibility and evidence/control at the retrieval boundary: 01-sessions-light.png, 03-people-light.png, and 06-people-dark-zh.png clearly lead with topic/person and retain the associated search context and recency. These pages do not present candidate scoring or external approval actions.

Read state and work attention remain distinct: 01-sessions-light.png shows read plus review attention; 02-sessions-unread-light.png adds explicit Unread; 05-sessions-dark-zh.png includes read/review-needed and unread/no-review-needed. review-input.md additionally reports native composition checks and CUA labels.

Credible accessibility layout: 07-sessions-ax5.png plus 09-sessions-ax5-scrolled.png reveal complete first-session review/recency content across positions; 08-people-ax5.png plus 10-people-ax5-scrolled.png reveal the next person's full identity and company/search context. Boundary-cut lines are not treated as inaccessible clipping. Menus remain visible for row starts. review-input.md reports native 44-point hittability with a numeric tolerance limited to 0.001 point.

System consistency: 01/03 and 05/06 retain the same retrieval controls across pages and themes. 04-people-filter.png visibly exposes scope, removal affordance, and the updated result count. The frozen input reports passing search/filter/reset, localized role query, restoration, and reduced-motion/menu checks; those reports support bounded platform confidence without proving VoiceOver or recovery conformance.

Visual craft is calm and coherent: no essential horizontal truncation is visible, sparse records remain honestly sparse, and separators/insets group records consistently. Separate five-category appearance score: 97/100 in mobile-craft.json; it does not raise the specialist behavior score to 4.
missing_evidence: No direct executable interaction, raw test-log inspection, VoiceOver sequence/user test, keyboard/focus sequence, or real-device ergonomic evidence was gathered by this reviewer. The reported native checks are attributed to round-3/review-input.md.

Retrieval loading, offline/error feedback, empty-result/reset transitions, interruptions, app termination, and complete recovery behavior are not depicted. The input reports reset and restoration success but does not turn the ten stills into complete state-matrix proof.

No small-phone, landscape, increased-contrast/reduce-transparency, RTL, or all-intermediate-Dynamic-Type image coverage. The input's reduced-motion/menu and contrast checks are useful partial evidence, not a complete accessibility certification.

No first-use explanation or measured find-and-reopen success, elapsed-time budget, field usefulness, seeded identity error correction, or external-effect audit. Storage/provenance and no-write guarantees are outside what these screenshots can establish. No observed veto is converted into an unconditional release pass.
